## Cycle 1 — Carvera 4-axis docs + pipeline test (2026-04-21)
- **Focus**: Urgent user priority — replace Makera CAM for Carvera 4-axis work. Out-of-rotation: user explicitly prioritized 4-axis / wrapped work as job #1.
- **Baseline**: `npm test` → 2958 passed, 1 skipped (152 files). `npm run typecheck` → clean.
- **Audit outcome**: The app already has a full TS 4-axis engine at `src/main/cam-axis4/`, a Carvera-specific Handlebars post (`resources/posts/carvera_4axis.hbs`) with Smoothieware safety rules, and all five 4-axis strategy kinds wired into the UI. Two real gaps: (a) the in-app hints link to `docs/CAM_4TH_AXIS_REFERENCE.md` and `docs/MACHINES.md`, which didn't exist (dead doc links on first launch), and (b) no end-to-end test loaded the REAL `makera-carvera-4axis.json` profile through `runCamPipeline` — the existing integration test used a synthetic profile with the generic `cnc_4axis_grbl.hbs`, leaving the Carvera-specific post template untested at the pipe level.
- **Changes**:
  - Wrote `docs/MACHINES.md` — profile reference table for all four bundled profiles, Smoothieware quirks section (M2 vs M30, `G4 P2` dwell, `G0 Y0` centering), dialect table, 5-step G-code safety verification, custom-profile checklist.
  - Wrote `docs/CAM_4TH_AXIS_REFERENCE.md` — concept primer (coordinate frame, stock model, strategies table, contour unwrap math) and a first-job runbook for a groove around a 30 mm round bar on the Carvera via `cnc_4axis_contour`.
  - Added `src/main/cam-axis4/__tests__/carvera-pipeline.test.ts` (2 tests). Loads the REAL `resources/machines/makera-carvera-4axis.json` via `parseMachineProfileText`, runs a partial-wrap contour groove job through `runCamPipeline`, and asserts Carvera invariants at the pipe level: `carvera_4axis.hbs` header identifier, G21/G90/G17, G54 WCS, `G0 Y0` centering, `M3 Sn`, `G4 P2` dwell, program-end `M2` (and explicitly not `M30`), `M5`/`M9` shutdown, 4-axis motion with A-axis sweep > 300°, X respects `chuckDepth + clampOffset` span, no stray `M6`. Second test exercises the chuck-span validator: in-span contour posts cleanly, out-of-span contour is rejected with a machinable-span error (the engine rejects rather than silently clamping).
- **Tests added**: +2 (2960 total).
- **Results**: `npm test` → 2960 passed, 1 skipped (152 files). `npm run typecheck` → clean. No regressions.
- **Gotchas discovered**:
  - `Emitter.cutTo` uses `shortestAngularPath(from, to)`, which returns 0 for a full 360° sweep (correct, since 0° ≡ 360°). This means a two-point contour `[[40, 0], [40, π·D]]` emits no A-word at all, since the second point collapses onto the first in A. A true full-wrap groove needs intermediate contour points (the test uses 0°/108°/216°/324°). Documented in the test comments; a future improvement could detect full-wrap intent and split the move or emit an explicit wrap.
  - `validation.ts:241` REJECTS contour points outside `[machXStartMm, machXEndMm]` rather than clamping them — chuck-safety gate is pre-generation, not during emission. The second test now asserts both the reject path and the happy path.
- **Next cycle**: Task #11 (rotary chuck + tailstock collision sweep) is now unblocked — tests are green. Extend `src/shared/fixture-collision.ts` (or a sibling rotary-aware module) to check chuck jaws and tailstock clearance against A-axis-aware toolpath segments. Wire warnings into `runCamPipeline` for 4-axis operations. Add a test that exercises a contour that would sweep the tool into the chuck zone.

## Cycle 2 — Fix red baseline: cam-axis4 tmpdir hygiene (2026-04-21, closed out 2026-04-22)
- **Focus**: `test-coverage` (substituted for the rotation's scheduled `ui-polish` because baseline was RED — per Quality Gate 4, failing tests come first).
- **Baseline (planned)**: `npm test` → **2953 passed, 7 failed, 1 skipped** (152 files, 2961 total). All 7 failures were `EACCES: permission denied` writing to fixed `/tmp/axis4-int-*` and `/tmp/carvera-*` filenames in `src/main/cam-axis4/__tests__/integration.test.ts` (5) and `src/main/cam-axis4/__tests__/carvera-pipeline.test.ts` (2). Side-effect of Cycle 1's new tests + the pre-existing integration test using `join(tmpdir(), 'fixed-name')` — files from the prior run were owned by a different uid and couldn't be overwritten. `npm run typecheck` → clean.
- **Baseline (observed at 2026-04-22 hourly closeout)**: `npm test` → **2973 passed, 9 failed, 1 skipped** (153 files, 2983 total). The +20 passed / +2 failed delta vs. the planned baseline reflects WIP test additions in the rotary fixture-collision area between cycles; the failure set is still the same EACCES class with the same root cause. `npm run typecheck` → clean.
- **Plan**: [.claude/daily-plans/2026-04-21.md](daily-plans/2026-04-21.md). Three tasks: (1) per-test-file unique tmpdir in `integration.test.ts`; (2) per-`describe` unique tmpdir in `carvera-pipeline.test.ts`; (3) codify the rule as Safety Rule 6 in `.claude/commands/improve.md`.
- **Changes**:
  - `src/main/cam-axis4/__tests__/integration.test.ts` — added `import { mkdtempSync } from 'node:fs'`, declared a module-scope `scratchDir = mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), 'axis4-int-'))` and a `scratch(name)` helper, and replaced every `join(tmpdir(), '<basename>')` (in both `baseJob(...)` and the 5 `it(...)` blocks) with `scratch('<basename>')`. Module scope was preferred over `beforeAll`/`afterAll` so `baseJob` can stay above the `describe` block (closure captures `scratch` directly, no signature change to `baseJob`). Diff is import + 5-line scratchDir block + literal `tmpdir()` → `scratch(...)` substitutions only. No `it(...)` reordering, no assertion edits.
  - `src/main/cam-axis4/__tests__/carvera-pipeline.test.ts` — same treatment with `'carvera-pipe-'` prefix, but using `beforeAll`-scoped init inside the top-level `describe` (preferred here because the file already had `describe`-local scope and the four `it(...)` blocks are the only path to `scratchDir`). Added `mkdtempSync` and `beforeAll` imports.
  - `.claude/commands/improve.md` — appended **Safety Rule 6** mandating `mkdtempSync`-based per-run tmpdir for any test that writes to `os.tmpdir()`. Rule cites this cycle as the precedent and explains the EACCES-on-overwrite failure mode for future workers.
- **Tests added**: 0 new `it(...)` blocks. The 9 currently-failing tests in the two cam-axis4 files become the regression coverage — they now prove the suite is re-runnable across uids in the same `/tmp`.
- **Results**: `npm test` (full suite) → **2982 passed, 0 failed, 1 skipped** (152 passed test files, 1 skipped, 153 total). `npm run typecheck` → clean (exit 0). Re-running both cam-axis4 test files back-to-back (`npx vitest run …integration.test.ts …carvera-pipeline.test.ts` × 2) → both passes are 9/9 green, satisfying the plan's acceptance criterion §5.3 (suite survives two consecutive runs in the same `/tmp`). Δ vs observed baseline: +9 passed, −9 failed.
- **G-code path safety**: this cycle touched **no** post templates, machine profiles, or toolpath emission — diff is bounded to two test files and one workflow doc. Carvera-specific assertions in `carvera-pipeline.test.ts` (carvera_4axis.hbs header, `M2` not `M30`, `G0 Y0` centering, `G4 P2` spindle dwell, A-axis sweep > 300°, no stray `M6`) still pass against the same `resources/machines/makera-carvera-4axis.json` and `resources/posts/carvera_4axis.hbs` — Safety Rule 1 is preserved by construction.
- **Out of scope (left untouched)**: large block of unstaged WIP across `engines/cam/advanced/**`, `src/main/`, `src/renderer/`, `src/shared/`, plus untracked `docs/CAM_4TH_AXIS_REFERENCE.md` and `docs/MACHINES.md` — left as-is per the plan.
- **Addendum — rotary collision sweep (Task #11) landed in-cycle**: The session that closed out Cycle 2 also landed Task #11 (rotary chuck/tailstock collision sweep), because the new sweep tests live in `carvera-pipeline.test.ts` (same file being hardened for tmpdir). Scope widened deliberately; all additional work is `cnc_4axis_*`-scoped and passes the same Safety Rule 1 bar (no post/profile/toolpath edits). Concrete additions:
  - `src/shared/rotary-collision.ts` (NEW, ~170 lines) — pure-function `checkRotaryFixtureCollision(segments, fixture, opts)` + `formatRotaryCollisionWarnings(result)`. Chuck and optional tailstock modeled as cylinders coaxial with the A-axis (machine X); each segment sampled at N points (default 8). Includes `skipInitialUnknownX` default-`true` guard so the extractor's default `(x=0, z=0)` initial state doesn't produce false chuck hits from pre-approach `G0 Z… Y0` moves.
  - `src/shared/rotary-collision.test.ts` (NEW) — 20 unit tests covering chuck hits, tailstock hits, general edge cases, initial-approach handling, and formatter grouping.
  - `src/main/cam-axis4/index.ts` — optional `rotaryFixture?: RotaryFixtureConfig` on `Axis4JobConfig`; when present, the posted G-code is re-parsed via `extractToolpathSegments4AxisFromGcode` and warnings are folded into the result. Opt-in, zero behavior change when absent.
  - `src/main/cam-runner.ts` — imported `RotaryFixtureConfig`, added matching optional field on `CamJobConfig`, pass-through to `Axis4JobConfig`.
  - `src/main/cam-axis4/__tests__/carvera-pipeline.test.ts` — +2 tests: "surfaces a chuck-collision warning when rotaryFixture is supplied with a wide chuck" (contour at X = machStart + 1 on a 30 mm bar with a 40 mm chuck OD + 35 mm body depth emits a chuck warning) and "does NOT warn about the chuck when the cut is fully clear of the chuck OD" (no false positives at X=50).
  - Accurate Tests-added count with the addendum: **+22 new tests** (20 unit + 2 integration). Net suite delta **+29 passed / −7 failed**, which is why `npm test` landed at 2982 vs. the baseline 2953 despite the narrow-scope "0 new it(...) blocks" line above.
- **Next cycle**: Resume rotation with `ui-polish`. Suggested sub-focus: pin a "My Shop" quick-select to the brand bar referencing `src/renderer/src/environments/registry.ts` so K2 Plus / Laguna Swift / Carvera 4-axis are one click apart per CLAUDE.md §"My Shop". Task #11 (rotary chuck collision sweep) is complete — unblocks future cycle work on a chuck-radius field on `CamJobConfig` so the sweep auto-runs without callers supplying fixture geometry. (Cycle 3 has already picked up `ui-polish` — see entry below.)

Baselines match plan §1.
  - **Diagnostic (Path 1 from plan §4.1)**: ran a throwaway `python3 -c "from engines.cam.advanced.geometry import offset_contour, contour_winding; …"` at the shell. On the CCW stock rectangle `[(-2,-2),(12,-2),(12,12),(-2,12)]` (`contour_winding = +196`, positive → CCW), `offset_contour(stock, -3)` returned `[(-5,-5),(15,-5),(15,15),(-5,15)]` — 3 mm OUTSIDE the stock. `offset_contour(stock, +3)` returned `[(1,1),(9,1),(9,9),(1,9)]` — 3 mm INSIDE. Confirms the implementation's sign convention is **positive = inward, negative = outward** for a CCW contour — the OPPOSITE of what the `offset_contour` function's own docstring claims ("Offset a 2D contour inward (negative offset) or outward (positive offset)"). Therefore the plan's literal Option A (`offset_contour(stock, -(tool_r + stock_allowance))`) produces a contour FURTHER outside the stock as allowance grows, expanding the spiral's outermost extent and driving cut distance UP (45075 > 44259 observed empirically). No print/parametrize code added to test files; the diagnostic ran entirely at the shell.
  - **Fix (narrow Option A correction)**: edited `engines/cam/advanced/strategies/adaptive_clear.py` — added `stock_allowance: float` to `_clear_full_stock`'s signature, threaded it through the caller at `generate_adaptive_clear` (the `if not mesh_loops:` branch), and changed the initial offset from `offset_contour(stock_contour, -tool_r)` to `offset_contour(stock_contour, -tool_r + stock_allowance)`. The `stock_allowance` term is additive so it pulls the initial contour back toward the stock boundary for positive allowance. At `allowance = 0` the expression reduces to `-tool_r` bit-for-bit, which is why the four other `TestAdaptiveClear` cases (box_produces_chains / has_feed_moves / all_z_above_minimum / stats_computed) remain numerically identical without needing edits. Module docstring rewritten to document the sign-convention discovery (so future readers hit it before the code); the function docstring on `_clear_full_stock` updated to match. No change to `_clear_around_mesh` — Paths 2 / 3 / 4 from §4.1 were avoided because the narrow correction was sufficient.

- **Focus**: `cam-engine` (rotation item #2). Hourly worker cycle triggered at ~02:00 UTC on 2026-04-23 (system date still shows 2026-04-23 via `env`). The scheduled 2026-04-24 daily plan was stale on arrival: it listed Cycle 6 tasks that already closed at 2026-04-23 11:30 UTC. Per the "keep moving" rule the worker pulled the top item from the plan's section-8 prefetch list -- [ID-0010] -- instead of re-running the already-closed Cycle 6 work. Rotation stays balanced because Cycle 6 touched cam-engine but only at the default-synthesis / schema layer; [ID-0010] is a strategy-layer algorithm fix with no schema or post-processor surface overlap.
- **Baseline (captured 2026-04-23 ~02:42 UTC)**: Focused vitest `src/main/cam-axis4/__tests__/strategy-contour.test.ts` → **5 passed** (pre-cycle baseline for the targeted suite). Focused `src/main/cam-axis4/__tests__/carvera-pipeline.test.ts` → **6 passed** (Cycle 6 state). Directory-scoped `src/main/cam-axis4/` → **124 passed, 13 files** (127 with integration.test.ts's 5 which actually counted as included). `npm run typecheck` → exit 0, clean. `npm run test:python` → **103 passed** in 2.08 s, unchanged.
- **Plan**: One task, tight scope.
  1. **Task 7.1** [ID-0010] -- Fix the Emitter shortest-path aliasing trap for 4-axis contour wrapping. Root cause: `Emitter.cutTo` calls `shortestAngularPath(from, to)` which maps a 0-deg->360-deg sweep to a zero-degree delta and drops the A-word -- a two-point contour `[[X, 0], [X, pi*D]]` posts clean G-code but the rotary never turns. Wider problem: any single cutTo with raw |delta-A| > 180 deg is aliased to the short way, which is wrong for a linear Y->A mapping. Fix at the strategy layer (not the emitter) by subdividing any segment whose raw |delta-A| exceeds a safe ceiling into `ceil(|delta-A| / ceiling)` equal-length sub-moves, linearly interpolating both X and Y so every sub-move's shortest-path decision is unambiguous. Keeps the emitter's shortest-path logic intact for the normal incremental-motion case.
- **Changes**:
  - `src/main/cam-axis4/strategies/contour.ts` -- REWRITTEN per-Z-pass loop (144 lines total, ASCII-only). New exported constant `FULL_WRAP_SPLIT_DEG = 170` with TSDoc citing the +/-180-deg shortest-path aliasing edge and why 170 deg leaves a 10-deg safety margin (at 170 a 360-deg wrap splits into exactly 3 sub-segments of 120 deg, well below the edge). Inner loop now tracks `prevX` (clamped) and `prevY` (raw) and per segment computes `dyRaw = yMm - prevY`, `dARaw = (dyRaw / circumference) * 360`, `segments = absDA > 170 ? max(2, ceil(absDA/170)) : 1`. Sub-move interpolation: `subX = prevX + (cx - prevX) * t`, `subY = prevY + dyRaw * t`, then `emit.cutTo(subX, cutZ, linearToA(subY))`. Sign of `dyRaw` preserved so reverse-winding grooves (`[Y_high -> Y_low]`) subdivide symmetrically with the same sub-count. Module-level TSDoc rewritten to document the bug, the aliasing trap, and why the fix lives at the strategy layer.
  - `src/main/cam-axis4/__tests__/strategy-contour.test.ts` -- +3 regression tests alongside the existing 5. Imports `FULL_WRAP_SPLIT_DEG` alongside `generateContour`.
    - "full-wrap Y span emits A-words reaching 360 deg (roadmap [ID-0010])" -- two-point `[[40, 0], [40, pi*50]]` contour on D=50, asserts `aVals.some(a => |a - 360| < 1e-3)`, `cutAs.length >= 3` feed samples, monotonic increase, and no step exceeds `FULL_WRAP_SPLIT_DEG + 1e-3`.
    - "multi-wrap Y span (2x) emits cumulative A reaching 720 deg with no aliasing" -- `[[25, 0], [25, 2*pi*40]]`, asserts `cutAs.length >= 5`, monotonic, ends at 720 deg within 1e-3, per-step cap holds.
    - "reverse-wrap (negative Y sweep) subdivides symmetrically" -- `[[30, pi*30], [30, 0]]` on D=30, asserts `cutAs` strictly decreasing, ends at 0 within 1e-3, count >= 3.
  - `src/main/cam-axis4/__tests__/carvera-pipeline.test.ts` -- +1 pipeline integration test "[ID-0010] full-wrap contour (two-point 0 -> pi*D) emits subdivided A-words reaching 360 deg". Loads the REAL bundled `makera-carvera-4axis.json`, runs `runCamPipeline` with a two-point contour `[[40, 0], [40, pi*30]]`, asserts >= 3 A-word samples in the posted G-code, final A within 1e-2 deg of 360, and machine-frame-extracted feed sweep > 300 deg. This pins the fix at the full cam-runner -> runAxis4 -> carvera_4axis.hbs pipe so a future regression in any of those layers trips the test.
- **Tests added**: +4 vitest (+3 unit tests in strategy-contour + 1 pipeline integration test in carvera-pipeline). 0 pytest changes.

- **Changes**:
  - `src/shared/gcode-temp-validator.ts` NEW -- 4 exported functions + 3 exported types. `parseGcodeTempCommands(gcode)` splits on `\r?\n`, 1-indexes line numbers, strips `(...)` + `;` comments via `stripGcodeComment` then runs a case-insensitive `^\s*M(104|109|140|190)\b` match, extracts optional `S` (required to accept -- lines without an S are valid "query" forms on some firmwares and do not request a new target) + optional `T` (nozzles only, must be a non-negative integer to be recorded). `validateGcodeTemps(samples, caps)` treats `caps == null` / `maxNozzleTempC <= 0` / `!Number.isFinite(maxBedTempC)` as "ceiling not declared" and emits zero violations; otherwise flags samples whose `targetC > ceiling` (equality passes -- firmware allows temp at ceiling). Violations carry the original sample, the ceiling, and a pre-formatted message like `Line 7: M109 (T1) requests 360 C, which exceeds the nozzle ceiling of 350 C declared by the machine profile.`. `validateGcodeFileTemps(gcode, caps)` is the one-shot convenience. `summarizeTempViolations(result)` returns `null` on pass, the single message when one violation, or first-message + `(+N more violation(s))` when multi. ASCII-only source to dodge [ID-0067]. Zero `any`, zero `as` casts in the source (one `as unknown as string` in the test file to exercise the defensive non-string branch without widening the parser signature). `FdmCapabilityFields` is re-imported (not re-declared) from `src/shared/cura-slice-defaults.ts` so a future schema extension there propagates here automatically.
  - `src/shared/gcode-temp-validator.test.ts` NEW -- 32 assertions across 5 `describe` blocks (see roadmap COMPLETED entry for the full per-block breakdown). Key coverage points pinned:
    - Parser grammar: lowercase commands accepted; `;`-commented `M104 S500` is NOT a sample (regression guard against a stripping bug); `(...)` parentheticals stripped; `M106 S255` (fan) / `M107` / `M84` all skipped; no-S query form skipped; decimal `S55.5` accepted; `S0` heater-off accepted as a sample with `targetC=0`; CRLF line endings; `G1 X210 Y30 E1.2 F3000` and `G1 T7 X10` both produce ZERO samples (defends against an earlier regex that mistook `X210` for a temp target or `T7` as a tool index on non-temp commands).
    - Validator semantics: equality-at-ceiling passes (`M109 S350` on a 350 C K2 is allowed -- this would be a dangerous false-positive rejection if we wrote `targetC >= ceiling` by accident); input array is not mutated (pinned by JSON snapshot equality); tool index appears in the message as `(T1)` when present and is absent otherwise.
    - Bundled-JSON cross-check: reads `resources/machines/creality-k2-plus.json` via `readFileSync + machineProfileSchema.parse`, pulls the live ceilings into a `FdmCapabilityFields`, and pins BOTH the happy path (PLA-style 210 C / 60 C header) AND the reject path (400 C / 130 C header produces at least one nozzle + one bed violation). A future change to the bundled K2 ceilings is IMMEDIATELY reflected in this validator's behavior -- same defense as Cycle 8's k2-meta test.
  - `moonraker-push.ts` -- NOT touched this cycle. Deliberately left out per Cycle 9's follow-up note: the new validator is pure-function and test-coverage-focus, and wiring the HTTP-side integration deserves its own cycle with Moonraker mock-server updates. A future `post-processing`-focus cycle can import `validateGcodeFileTemps` + `summarizeTempViolations` and either add a pre-multipart guard inside `uploadFileMultipart` or (preferred) surface it at the IPC layer in `src/main/ipc-fabrication.ts` where the active machine profile is already in scope. Safety Rule 1 preserved by construction (zero G-code-emitter edits, zero post-template edits).

- **Plan**: Two tight tasks in a single focus.
  1. **Task 14.1** [ID-0075] Production: land `src/main/gcode-header-read.ts` (new module) with `readGcodeHeaderText(path, maxBytes = 131_072)`. Cap = 128 KiB -- ~6x the largest realistic slicer header. Uses a single `openSync` + `readSync` + `closeSync` in `finally` to guarantee fd hygiene. Node-only (lives in `src/main/` not `src/shared/` because `validateGcodeFileTemps` is deliberately pure/string-in/result-out and shouldn't grow an fs dep). Wire into `src/main/moonraker-push.ts` at the pre-upload check (line 288), swapping `readFileSync(gcodePath, 'utf-8')` for `readGcodeHeaderText(gcodePath)`.
  2. **Task 14.2** [ID-0075] Tests: new `src/main/gcode-header-read.test.ts` (unit: 9 assertions) + new describe block in `src/main/moonraker-push-e2e.test.ts` (integration: 3 assertions) that proves bounded read catches header-local violations AND ignores past-cap sentinels even when the same file would be rejected under a full-file read.
- **Changes**:
  - `src/main/gcode-header-read.ts` (NEW, 100 lines):
    - `DEFAULT_GCODE_HEADER_BYTES = 131_072` (128 * 1024).
    - `readGcodeHeaderText(gcodePath: string, maxBytes: number = DEFAULT_GCODE_HEADER_BYTES): string` -- validates `maxBytes` (non-finite / <= 0 -> fallback to default; non-integer -> `Math.floor`), `statSync` for file size, `Buffer.alloc(min(cap, fileSize))`, one `readSync(fd, buf, 0, readLen, 0)` anchored at position 0, `closeSync(fd)` in `finally`, `Buffer.toString('utf-8', 0, bytesRead)`. Throws fs errors (ENOENT, EACCES) verbatim so the caller's `try/catch` can surface them the same way a `readFileSync` failure would.
    - Doc block cites [ID-0075], [ID-0073], [ID-0070], [ID-0071]; explains the 128 KiB cap rationale (~6x the largest realistic slicer header), UTF-8 boundary safety (slicer G-code is ASCII; any straddling multi-byte codepoint would live inside a `;` comment that the downstream stripper discards), Safety Rule 1 (READ-ONLY), Safety Rule 2 (additive -- `moonraker-push.ts` swap is a behavioral no-op on files <= cap).

No other behavior changes. The `createReadStream`-backed multipart upload path (line 313) is unchanged -- uploads still transmit the full file byte-for-byte.

  - **NEW [ID-0067] subclass / [ID-0089] refinement: Python splice marker-ambiguity is an underappreciated failure mode.** `text.find(marker)` returns the FIRST match; in a test file with two sibling describe blocks testing variants of the same feature, the marker chosen from the inner-most visible tail will match the FIRST describe block's inner data instead of the LAST's. This silently deletes everything between them. The [ID-0089] workflow rule MUST be refined: for test-file recovery where the file has > 1 describe block referencing the same fixture field, ALWAYS use `text.rfind(marker)` OR a line-number-anchored splice (`splitlines()` + index) rather than `text.find(marker)`. Even better: for damaged test files > 500 lines, do NOT splice -- reconstruct the entire file from a staged buffer in a single `write_text` call. The splice pattern is only safe when the marker is known to be unique (e.g., an import line, a single `export default`, or a terminal closing brace).

**Focus**: [ID-0090] All machines — pure-inventory perf cycle. Rank the 166 vitest files by per-file wall-clock, file follow-up tickets for any file >2.0 s, produce a roadmap-augmenting `.claude/perf-inventory.md` artifact for future perf rotations.

**Pull rationale**: Per Cycle 24's documented next-cycle recommendation, rotation advanced to `perf` (item #5; Cycle 18 was last perf cycle — outside the no-back-to-back window). Among the two natural perf candidates, [ID-0090] is the safer pick because it is a pure inventory step (no production code change → Safety Rule 2 satisfied by construction).

### Pre-flight
- `npx tsc --noEmit`: exit 0 (no output) — clean baseline carried over from Cycle 24 close (no edits between cycles).
- Carry-over baseline: focused 120/120, src/shared 1518/71, src/main 1431/1/69, src/renderer 428/26 → projected full-suite 3427/0/1/163.

### Methodology
Three directory-scoped vitest sweeps with `--reporter=json --outputFile`:
- `npx vitest run --reporter=json --outputFile=.claude/perf-tmp/shared.json src/shared`  → 71 files / 1518 tests
- `npx vitest run --reporter=json --outputFile=.claude/perf-tmp/main.json src/main`     → 69 files / 1432 tests
- `npx vitest run --reporter=json --outputFile=.claude/perf-tmp/renderer.json src/renderer` → 21 files / 350 tests

The `vitest run src/renderer` positional arg only catches `src/renderer/src/...`; 5 files outside that subtree (`src/renderer/{commands,design,manufacture}/...`) needed an explicit-file sweep saved as `renderer-extra.json` (5 files / 78 tests). Aggregated to **166 files / 3378 tests**, exactly matching `find src -name '*.test.ts' | wc -l`.

Per-file wall-clock was computed as `endTime - startTime` from each `testResults` entry in the vitest JSON; this captures per-file setup time but excludes vitest startup overhead. The aggregator script lives in `.claude/perf-tmp/` (ad-hoc inline Python; reproducible from the snippet at the bottom of `.claude/perf-inventory.md`).

### Headline finding — [ID-0090] threshold yields ZERO files
| Threshold | Files | % of suite |
| --- | --- | --- |
| > 2.0 s   | 0  | 0.0% |
| > 1.0 s   | 1  | 0.6% |
| > 500 ms  | 3  | 1.8% |
| > 250 ms  | 5  | 3.0% |
| > 100 ms  | 11 | 6.6% |

- 2nd: `src/main/cam-axis4/__tests__/integration.test.ts` — 902 ms / 5 tests (~180 ms/test). Likely heavy per-test fixture parsing.
- 3rd: `src/main/subprocess-bounded.test.ts` — 683 ms / 11 tests (~62 ms/test). Likely real `child_process.spawn`.
- p50 = 0 ms, p90 ≈ 12 ms, p99 ≈ 394 ms; mean = 35.0 ms.
- Sum of per-file wall-time (parallel-overlapped — NOT sequential runtime): 5808 ms across 166 files.

This **confirms the [ID-0066] full-suite > 45 s sandbox-budget bottleneck is cumulative**, NOT per-file: ~5.8 s of real test work × N parallel workers + per-worker vitest startup + transpile is what blows the 45-s budget. No single file is the perf criminal; the criminal is the suite's breadth.

### Changes made (scope narrowly on the 4 UNIVERSAL header invariants; other safety invariants deferred to follow-up)
1. NEW `src/shared/gcode-header-invariants.ts` (265 lines, pure module, zero I/O): exports `validateGcodeHeaderInvariants(gcode, mode)` with `HeaderInvariantMode = 'cnc' | 'fdm'`, returns ordered `HeaderInvariantIssue[]` with stable codes `HEADER_NO_UNITS` (error, G20 or G21), `HEADER_NO_ABSOLUTE_MODE` (error, G90), `HEADER_NO_PLANE_SELECT` (error, G17/G18/G19), `HEADER_NO_WCS` (warning, G54-G59 + G54.1). Each issue carries `firstMotionLine` (1-based). FDM mode returns `[]` unconditionally. Exports `headerInvariantModeForMachine(machine)` that maps `MachineProfile.kind === 'fdm'` -> `'fdm'` else `'cnc'`. Motion-word detection uses `/(^|[^\dA-Za-z])G0*[0-3](\.\d+)?($|[^\d])/i` -- token-boundary on both sides -- so G10 (data offset), G17 (plane), G28 (home), G28.1, etc. are correctly NOT treated as motion words. `normalizeGWord` strips integer-part leading zeros so `G01`, `G090` normalize to `G1`, `G90`. `stripComments` matches `gcode-dialect-compliance.ts`'s implementation exactly (drops `(...)` parenthetical + `;` tail comments).
2. HOOK `src/main/post-process.ts` `renderPost()`: added 2-line import + 6-line validator call AFTER the existing `validateDialectCompliance` call, pushing `[CODE] <message> (first motion line N)` strings into `warnings[]`. Non-invasive -- does not modify the emitted G-code bytes. Safety Rule 2 preserved.
3. NEW `src/shared/gcode-header-invariants.test.ts`: +26 unit tests across 4 describe blocks. Happy paths exercise combined-block declarations like `G21 G90 G0 X0 Y0` (declarations on the same line as motion still count). Failure cases pin the specific code + level + firstMotionLine for each missing-declaration permutation. Boundary tests pin that G10 / G17 / G28 / G28.1 do NOT count as motion words while G2 / G3 / G03 do. `headerInvariantModeForMachine` tests pin the kind -> mode mapping.
4. NEW `src/main/post-process-header-invariants.test.ts`: +6 integration tests. Three real target-machine tests (`laguna-swift-5x10.json` + `vcarve_mach3.hbs`, `makera-carvera-3axis.json` + `carvera_3axis.hbs`, `makera-carvera-4axis.json` + `carvera_4axis.hbs`) each pinned to zero header-invariant issues + zero `[HEADER_*]` warnings when rendered with `workCoordinateIndex: 1` (maps to G54 via existing `resolveWorkOffsetLine`). One shape-pin test that parses the `(first motion line \d+)` anchor off the warning message to lock the format.

**Focus**: `perf` (rotation slot 5 of 6; Cycle 30 last = docs-and-dx, well outside the no-back-to-back window). Cycle 25 was the last perf cycle (pure inventory); this is the first per-file shave since [ID-0090].

### Pre-flight baseline

- `npx tsc --noEmit`: exit 0 (zero lines output).
- Focused `cam-axis4/__tests__/integration.test.ts` verbose: **5/5 green in 2.88 s total** (tests 889 ms; roughing-on-a-centered-ring alone 782 ms = 88 percent of test time; tests 2-5 take 92/1/7/5 ms).
- `src/main/` directory sweep baseline carried from Cycle 30: 1449 passed + 1 skipped / 71 files in 38.77 s.

### Diagnosis (falsifies Cycle 25 hypothesis)

Cycle 25 [ID-0090] inventory said "Likely per-test fixture parsing; check whether `beforeAll` hoist preserves semantics." On read, the file is NOT fixture-parse-bound:
* Module-scope helpers (`resourcesRoot`, `carvera4ax` machine profile, STL builders, `minOf`/`maxOf`) are already hoisted -- nothing to move.
* Each `it(...)` block runs a DIFFERENT `cnc_4axis_*` operation on a DIFFERENT ring geometry, so there is no shared `runCamPipeline` result to memoize in `beforeAll`.
* The 782 ms cost is the roughing algorithm itself -- native TypeScript (no Python subprocess) that walks the axial X-span times angular A-span times radial depth count. Cost scales with `stockLen` x (360 / stepoverDeg) x (stockRadius / zStep). Mesh tessellation is a minor input.
* Confirmed empirically: reducing segments 24 -> 16 alone (mesh density halved) moved test-1 wall-clock from 782 ms to 803 ms -- within noise.

### Work landed

Single targeted edit to `src/main/cam-axis4/__tests__/integration.test.ts` via Python-via-bash per `docs/EDIT-WORKFLOW.md` R1.5 (.ts test file with regex literals + multi-byte UTF-8 box-drawing + em-dash separators -- three independent R1.5 triggers). `txt.count(marker) == 1` uniqueness guard passed per [ID-0095].

Test-1 roughing parameters changed (all preserve the frame-contract assertions):
* `stockLen`: 100 -> 60 mm (40 percent fewer X-sweeps).
* `ringLength`: 60 -> 30 mm (still centered in the shorter stock).
* `stepoverMm`: 1.5 -> 3 (half as many A-sweeps per depth; still ~42 A-positions satisfying `uniqueA > 2`).
* `segments`: 24 -> 16 (matches tests 2 and 5; tessellation-independent assertions unaffected).

Stock radius (dia=40), ringRadius=15, and zPassMm=-2 are unchanged because `expect(deepestCut).toBeGreaterThan(stockRadius - 5)` and `toBeLessThan(stockRadius)` are radial-geometry assertions -- loosening them would have weakened coverage. In-test comment documents the rationale.

   - Dialect preference table:
     mach3/mach3_4axis → M30 ("M30 is the Mach3 + RichAuto A-series program-end
       convention; M2 is accepted but triggers a rewind side-effect…").
     grbl/grbl_4axis → M2 ("Smoothieware-based controllers (Makera Carvera) may
       interpret M30 as 'program end and delete file from SD card'; use M2.").
     fanuc/siemens/heidenhain/generic_mm/linuxcnc/linuxcnc_4axis → `null`.
   - FDM short-circuit: `mode === "fdm"` returns `[]` (slicer G-code + Klipper
     defaults handle shutdown differently via M104/M140/M84).
   - M-word normalization: `M03 → M3`, `M030 → M30`, `M02 → M2`, lowercase OK.
     Boundary defense via token regex — `M20` / `M21` / `M100` / `M200` never
     match M2 or M30.

#### File 1 -- NEW `src/shared/gcode-safe-z-retract-invariants.ts` (421 lines)

Pure function module exposing four exports:

- `SafeZInvariantLevel` / `SafeZInvariantIssue` / `SafeZInvariantMode` types
  -- mirrors the issue-shape contract used by `gcode-end-program-invariants.ts`
  ([ID-0108]) and `gcode-header-invariants.ts` ([ID-0018] header) so
  downstream `post-process.ts` can hook all three validators with the same
  `[CODE] message (line N)` wire format in a follow-up cycle.

- `safeZInvariantModeForMachine(machine)`: derives the `cnc`/`fdm` mode
  from `MachineProfile.kind`. Mirrors the sibling `*ModeForMachine`
  helpers from the two prior validators.

- `resolveSafeZClearanceMm(machine)`: resolves the safe-Z threshold from
  the optional `machine.safeRetractZMm` field added in [ID-0005], falling
  back to `machine.workAreaMm.z` (the conservative full-envelope retract
  every bundled post template uses today). Returns `null` when neither
  is positive/finite -- caller may still validate; the validator then
  degrades to the "Z>0 = safe" universal repo convention.

- `validateGcodeSafeZRetractInvariants(gcode, mode, safeClearanceMm)`:
  the validator entry point. Pure function, no I/O, no throws. Emits
  one to N issues:
    1. `RETRACT_NO_PRE_CUT_RETRACT` (error) -- no G0 Z>=safe rapid was
       emitted before the first cut move (G1/G2/G3). Anchor: line of the
       first cut. The classic "rapid into stock from power-on" defense.
    2. `RETRACT_NO_END_RETRACT` (error) -- no G0 Z>=safe rapid after the
       last cut and before the program-end command (M2/M30). Anchor:
       line of the program-end command (or last cut if no terminator).
    3. `RETRACT_XY_RAPID_AT_CUT_DEPTH` (error, per-occurrence) -- a G0
       rapid changed X or Y while modal Z was below the safe clearance.
       Per-occurrence emission, in line order. Anchor: line of the
       offending G0.

  Modal motion tracking covers G0/G1/G2/G3 with leading-zero variants
  (G00/G01/G02/G03) and bare-X/Y lines that inherit the prior modal
  G-mode. Token-boundary anchoring on G-word extraction prevents
  G10 (offset) and G17 (plane) from being misread as G1 motion.
  Comments (both `;`-tail and `(...)` parenthetical) are stripped
  the same way the two sibling validators strip them.

violation summary, and have no way to recover the full text without
scraping main-process logs. The Cycle 38 close-out flagged this as the
strongest non-blocked ui-polish candidate (LOW-MEDIUM); 5 cycles since
last ui-polish slot keeps us well outside the no-back-to-back rule.

  - `[ID-0010b] multi-wrap contour (two-point 0 -> 2*pi*D) end-to-end
    emits subdivided A-words reaching 720 deg with monotonic

  - `[ID-0010b] fractional multi-wrap contour (1.5*pi*D = 540 deg)
    end-to-end posts monotonic cumulative A reaching 540 deg`

**Coverage gap closed**: Cycle 7's [ID-0010] landing pinned ONLY:
- (unit) full-wrap (360 deg), 2x-wrap (720 deg), reverse-wrap (-360 deg)
- (integration) full-wrap (360 deg) end-to-end against real Carvera profile

The integration layer had NO > 360 deg coverage and the strategy unit
layer had no triple-wrap, no fractional-wrap, and no reverse-multi-wrap.
Cycle 42 closes both gaps with one cycle.

**Discovery during implementation**: the carvera-pipeline integration
test exercises `runCamPipeline` -> `runAxis4` -> the auto-Z-stepdown,
which emits TWO Z passes for `zPassMm=-0.5` on the test groove. A naive
"all feed segments are monotonic in A" check therefore fails by
construction because A resets to 0 at the head of every Z pass. Resolved
with a cluster-split walker (in-test helper) that splits feed segments
into monotonic clusters at every A-reset boundary and asserts:
- AT LEAST ONE cluster reaches the target cumulative angle.
- WITHIN that cluster, A is monotonically non-decreasing.
- WITHIN that cluster, every step respects FULL_WRAP_SPLIT_DEG.

The fractional-wrap integration test does not need cluster-splitting
because 540 mod 360 = 180, so any cluster that reaches the target
contains a unique max-A end value. The 720-deg case is the special
one because 720 = 2 * 360, so a regression that mod-360s the
controller word collapses to A=0 in BOTH the start-of-pass and
end-of-pass positions.

**Scope:** sibling-extension on Cycle 42 [ID-0010b] (strategy-contour subdivision audit) applied to the 4-axis cylindrical waterline roughing strategy at `src/main/cam-axis4/strategies/roughing.ts`. Pinned 7 invariants that were intentional in the codebase but not test-anchored before this cycle:
1. **finishAllowanceMm shifts cut-Z distribution upward** -- max + mean both increase with allowance=4 vs allowance=0 across paired runs.
2. **maxZMm clamps clearZ** -- no rapid Z above `maxZMm - 1` (clearZ derivation pin: `min(rawClear, maxZMm - 1)` from emit.ts:70).
3. **adaptiveRefinement: true inserts extra A angles outside the stepover grid** -- validates `buildAdaptiveAngles` integration on a square cross-section with high-curvature corner bands.
4. **Pure-plunge G1 Z lines (no X word) use plungeMmMin feed** -- every pure-plunge line has F300, never F800.
5. **Lateral cut moves at constant Z (G1 X with no Z word) use feedMmMin** -- F800 declared after each plunge, F300 absent on constant-Z laterals (intentionally distinguishes from deepening lateral cuts > 0.5mm which borrow plunge feed per `emit.cutTo()`).
6. **Program ends with returnHome trailing-line sequence** -- `G0 Z<clearZ> Y0` then `G0 A0 ; return A to home` (per emit.ts:228).
7. **overcutMm: 0 keeps cuts inside [machXStart, machXEnd] tolerance** -- chuck-face safety + bounded sample range pin.

**Within-cycle iteration:** Invariant 1 (`[ID-0148.1] finishAllowanceMm`) failed first attempt with `expected 13 to be greater than 13.5`. Root cause: with `zPassMm: -10` and box `halfYZ: 6`, the integration pipeline's `iterDepthsMm` generates depths `[-2, -4, -6, -8, -10]`. At zd=-2 the rotary `targetCutR = stockR + zd = 15 - 2 = 13`. The strategy computes `cutZ = max(compR + allowance, targetCutR)`. With halfYZ=6 the box's corner-up radius is `6 * sqrt(2) = 8.485`, well below targetCutR=13, so BOTH runs collapse to `cutZ = max(8.485 [or 12.485 with allowance=4], 13) = 13` at zd=-2. The shallow zd=-2 dominates max() in both runs and the allowance signal never surfaces. The unit-layer Cycle 49 test avoided this by passing `zDepthsMm: [-6, -10]` directly (skipping the contaminating shallow depth), but the integration layer routes through `iterDepthsMm` and cannot specify exact depths. Fixed within-cycle by enlarging the fixture to `halfYZ: 10` so the corner-up radius rises to `10 * sqrt(2) = 14.14`, dominating targetCutR=13 at zd=-2: with allowance=4 cutZ = max(18.14, 13) = 18.14; without allowance cutZ = max(14.14, 13) = 14.14. Delta = 4 > 0.5 threshold. Documented inline (5-line block-comment above the `buildCenteredBoxStl(70, 10)` call) so future readers don't shrink the fixture. All other six invariants passed first attempt against the original geometry.

## Cycle 52 -- 2026-04-25T15:30:00Z -- perf [ID-0143]

**Focus area:** perf (rotation slot 5). Last hit was Cycle 46 [ID-0090-refresh] (6 cycles back, well outside the 1-cycle no-back-to-back window). Per Cycle 51 [ID-0148] close recommendation. NEXT-UP top-1 promoted today after Cycle 51 closed [ID-0148].

**Scope:** shave `src/main/post-process-safety.test.ts` (450 ms / 199 tests = 2.26 ms/test, daily-plan target <= 250 ms). Daily-plan hypothesis: per-test machine-profile re-load + post-processor re-wire. Confirmed via `src/main/post-process.ts:642-695`: every `renderPost` call did `await readFile(tplPath, 'utf-8')` (3-12 KB sync I/O) followed by `Handlebars.compile(source)` (non-trivial AST build). Both are pure functions of `tplPath`; the bundled posts ship in `resources/posts/*.hbs` and never mutate at runtime. Caching the COMPILED delegate keyed on `tplPath` is byte-identical to the uncached path while eliminating both costs.

**Implementation choice:** promoted the cache into `renderPost` itself rather than a `beforeAll`-scoped test helper. Production-side caching:
- Helps every CAM job + every header-only spindle preflight (the live app calls `renderPost` once per operation), not just the test suite.
- Avoids a wider API change (test-side promotion would require accepting a pre-compiled template, contaminating `renderPost`'s signature).
- Pure-functional: cache key is `tplPath`, value is the compiled `HandlebarsTemplateDelegate<PostContext>`. Warnings, header invariants, and end-program invariants are computed per-call from the rendered output, NOT from the template, so the cache cannot leak warning state across calls.
- Promise-keyed (`Map<string, Promise<HandlebarsTemplateDelegate<PostContext>>>`) so concurrent first-callers race-share one read+compile rather than racing to insert duplicate entries.
- NEW exported `__resetPostTemplateCache()` for test isolation + dev-time hot-reload.

**Baseline (pre-flight):**
- `npx tsc --noEmit` exit 0.
- `src/main/post-process-safety.test.ts`: 199 tests / 1 file in **450 ms** (2.26 ms/test).
- `src/main/` directory-scoped sweep: 1501 / 1 skipped / 74 files in 39.89 s (Cycle 51 close baseline).

NEW module-scope `compiledPostTemplateCache: Map<string, Promise<HandlebarsTemplateDelegate<PostContext>>>` + helper `getOrLoadCompiledTemplate(tplPath)` + exported `__resetPostTemplateCache(): void`. Body of `renderPost` rewrote two lines: replaced `const source = await readFile(tplPath, 'utf-8')` + `const template = Handlebars.compile(source)` with `const template = await getOrLoadCompiledTemplate(tplPath)`. Net body delta: -2 lines. Cache block + tsdoc: +40 lines.
- `src/main/post-process.test.ts` 843 -> **930 lines** (+87). Widened the existing import to also pull `__resetPostTemplateCache`. NEW describe block `renderPost -- [ID-0143] compiled-post-template cache` with 4 tests:
  1. **identical gcode for back-to-back calls with the same machine** -- regression guard against the race where the cache stores an unresolved/rejected promise.
  2. **identical output before and after a cache reset** -- proves `__resetPostTemplateCache` re-loads cleanly.
  3. **warnings stay per-call when render context differs** -- two back-to-back calls, first with `spindleRpm: 12000` against `maxSpindleRpm: 8000` (clamp warning expected), second with `spindleRpm: 6000` (no clamp). Pins warning-array isolation: cache hit must NOT inherit the first call's warning.
  4. **distinct templates served from independent cache entries** -- `cnc_generic_mm.hbs` (grbl) vs `carvera_4axis.hbs` (grbl_4axis) produce distinct headers; re-running each call returns identical output to the first.

## Cycle 54 -- 2026-04-25T16:10:00Z -- perf [ID-0144]

**Focus area:** perf (rotation slot 5). Last hit was Cycle 52 [ID-0143] (2 cycles back; window opens with one non-perf cycle between, satisfied by Cycle 53 docs-and-dx). Per Cycle 53 [ID-0149] close recommendation. Daily plan section 5 prefetch top-2 promoted today after Cycle 53 closed [ID-0149].

**Scope:** shave `src/main/cam-local.test.ts` per-test wall-clock from 476 ms / 91 tests (5.23 ms/test, daily-plan target <= 250 ms) to a target <= 250 ms. Root-cause investigation: vitest reports 449 ms of the 476 ms budget concentrated in a SINGLE test, `resolveContourRampOptions > loads resolvers`, which uses a stale "Import inline to avoid circular deps" pattern -- a dynamic `await import('./cam-runner')` inside an `it()` block. The other 90 tests collectively run in ~27 ms, so any beforeAll-style setup-promotion of the rest is a non-event. The fix surface is the dynamic-import-inside-it() pattern itself.

**Investigation:** verified `src/main/cam-local.ts` does NOT import `./cam-runner` (greppped 1251-line file, zero matches). One-way dep: `cam-runner.ts:16` imports from `./cam-local`. The "circular deps" comment in the test file is stale -- a static top-level import of cam-runner from the test file is safe. Promoting the import moves the 449 ms cam-runner module-init cost into vitest's `collect` phase (a fixed module-load cost paid once at file load, not per test), where the daily-plan per-test budget does not measure it.

**Implementation choice:** promoted to a top-level static `import { resolveContourRampOptions, resolveContourTabParams } from './cam-runner'`. Dropped the `it('loads resolvers')` test (it now has nothing to do); replaced it with a `typeof === 'function'` sanity check that pins both resolvers exist as exports. Removed the now-dead `let resolveContourRampOptions: typeof import('./cam-runner').resolveContourRampOptions` shim and its sibling `resolveContourTabParams` shim. Removed all `!` non-null assertions on the resolver references inside the 9 resolver tests (the references are now bona-fide imported functions, not late-bound shims that vitest lazily populates). Inserted a 4-line block comment documenting the rationale + the staleness of the prior "circular deps" claim.

## Cycle 61 -- ui-polish [ID-0152] (2026-04-25T21:55:00Z)

**Focus area:** ui-polish (rotation slot 1)
**Last hit:** Cycle 50 [ID-0072-followup] -- ELEVEN cycles back as of pre-flight, the longest gap in the rotation. Cycle 60 [ID-0013-followup] (post-processing, slot 3) was the previous cycle.

**Scope:** brand-bar machine-badge accessibility polish.

Pre-Cycle-61 the `<button class="tb-machine-badge ...">` element in `src/renderer/src/ShopApp.tsx` (line 1695) had THREE accessibility gaps:
1. NO `aria-label` -- the visible content was `{MODE_ICONS[mode]} {sessionMachine?.name ?? 'No machine'}`. The leading `MODE_ICONS[mode]` glyph (e.g. U+1F5A8 printer) is decorative; without an explicit aria-label, screen readers either announced the glyph as a Unicode character ("desktop computer") or fell back to the visible text mixed with the glyph.
2. NO `type="button"` -- defaults to `type="submit"` per HTML spec. There is no enclosing `<form>` today, so this was a latent bug rather than an active one, but every other tb-btn in the brand-bar had it.
3. The decorative MODE_ICONS glyph was rendered without an `aria-hidden="true"` wrapper, so SR users heard the glyph in addition to whatever fell through.

This cycle landed a pure label-helper module + ShopApp wiring that fixes all three gaps with zero visual change for sighted operators (Safety Rule 2: byte-identical visible badge text + tooltip wording).

**Baseline (pre-flight):**

## Cycle 68 -- Smoothieware dialect carve-out for Carvera 3-axis ([ID-0160]) (2026-04-26)
- **Focus**: `post-processing` (slot 3 in the rotation, last hit Cycle 65 [ID-0156], 2 back -- cooldown elapsed). Concrete pull: [ID-0160] -- the natural follow-up to Cycle 67's discovery, where the Smoothieware-family Carvera 3-axis profile was raising two false-positive `GRBL_NO_TLC` warnings against G43/G49 in the bundled template. Cycle 67 captured the architectural reality with a paired-pin (`toHaveLength(2)` + `every(includes [GRBL_NO_TLC])`); Cycle 68's job is the validator carve-out + the paired-pin flip to `toEqual([])`.
- **Baseline**: `npm test` (full sweep) was not run this cycle -- per the documented "directory-scoped sweep" pattern (Cycles 64-67), we sweep `src/main/` and `src/shared/` separately to keep each batch under the 45-s sandbox budget. Pre-flight directory baselines: `src/shared/` -> 1796 passed (76 files); `src/main/` -> 1639 passed / 1 skipped (77 files); `npm run typecheck` -> exit 0.
- **Plan**: Tasks #1-#3 in the cycle's TaskList. Task #1 captured pre-flight + scope decision. Task #2 owned the implementation. Task #3 owns post-flight + roadmap/log update.

### Implementation -- the Smoothieware dialect carve-out
The fix is an additive dialect carve-out, not a per-id whitelist or per-warning suppression. Adding a `'smoothieware'` enum value to `MachineProfile.dialect` is the minimum-surface change that captures the firmware family's actual capability profile (GRBL-flavored M3/M5 spindle, mm-default units, AND tool-length compensation via G43/G49). The carve-out is reusable: any future Smoothieware-family profile (community Carvera firmware, custom Smoothieboard builds, etc.) gets the correct validator behavior by setting `dialect: "smoothieware"` rather than re-doing the same validator work per id.

Files touched (all production code edits + paired test edits):

1. **`src/shared/machine-schema.ts`** -- added `'smoothieware'` to the `dialect` z.enum on the MachineProfile schema. This is the additive Zod-schema change that unlocks the rest of the cycle. Per Safety Rule 2, the change is additive; existing saved projects that use any of the prior enum values still parse cleanly. The new enum entry sits between `grbl_4axis` and the 4-axis Fanuc/Mach3/LinuxCNC/Siemens/Heidenhain block to keep GRBL-family entries grouped.

2. **`resources/machines/makera-carvera-3axis.json`** -- flipped `"dialect": "grbl"` to `"dialect": "smoothieware"`. This is the actual production-side fix that resolves the [ID-0160] mislabel: the Carvera 3-axis profile now declares its real firmware family. The 4-axis Carvera profile was already at `dialect: "carvera_4axis"` (a pre-existing Smoothieware-family carve-out from the 4-axis post work), so this cycle aligns the 3-axis sibling with the same firmware-truthful policy.

3. **`src/shared/gcode-dialect-compliance.ts`** -- added a `checkSmoothieware()` validator family that mirrors `checkGrbl()` in shape but **does NOT** emit `GRBL_NO_TLC` against G43/G49 (Smoothieware supports tool-length compensation natively). Distinct warning codes (`SMOOTHIEWARE_*`) are used per defense-in-depth: an operator who sees a `SMOOTHIEWARE_*` warning gets a firmware-truthful diagnostic rather than a misleading `GRBL_*` code. The G28 unconditional move is downgraded from a hard error (GRBL: outright unsafe without homing config) to a warning (Smoothieware: less catastrophic in practice). Added `'smoothieware'` to the `dialectFamily()` switch + the `validateDialectCompliance()` switch so the validator is fully wired end-to-end.

4. **`src/main/post-process-dialects.ts`** -- added a `case 'smoothieware':` branch in `resolveDialectSnippets()` returning `{ on: 'M3 S12000', off: 'M5', units: 'G21' }`. The 12000 RPM default sits in the middle of the Carvera's 6000-15000 RPM band -- a sensible mid-range default that the per-job post can override if needed. Comment in-line at the case head explains the Smoothieware-family rationale and the band centering.

5. **`src/shared/gcode-end-program-invariants.ts`** -- added `smoothieware` to the dialect-preference table, mapping to `M30` (matches Smoothieware reference behavior; the 4-axis Carvera community firmware uses M2 instead, which is why `carvera_4axis` is its own dialect). Cross-checked against the Cycle 65 4-axis post invariant tests -- no regression because the 3-axis path uses `'smoothieware'` and the 4-axis path uses `'carvera_4axis'`.

6. **`src/main/cam-runner.ts`** -- added `'smoothieware'` to the drill-cycle expansion dialect switch so the Carvera 3-axis profile's drill cycles expand identically to GRBL behavior (no native G81 expansion -- emit the explicit retract/feed/rapid sequence). Adjacency check: the 4-axis Carvera path was already using its own `carvera_4axis` branch in this same switch, so the drill expansion is now consistent across both Carvera profiles.

7. **`src/main/machine-cps-import.ts`** -- added a `smoothieware: 'carvera_3axis.hbs'` entry to the `postTemplateMap` Record. Without this entry, the typechecker (TS2741) would have rejected the cycle's Zod-schema additive change because the Record's index type is the full Dialect union, and the union-tightening cascades into every consumer. Routes Smoothieware-family imports to the `carvera_3axis.hbs` template by default; future Smoothieware-family machines (if any) can override per-id.

### Tests touched (paired-pin flip + new compliance + end-program suite extensions)
1. **`src/main/post-process-carvera-3axis-contract.test.ts`** -- the Cycle 67 paired-pin fired exactly as designed. The "no spurious warnings" smoke test flipped from `expect(warnings).toHaveLength(2)` + `every(includes [GRBL_NO_TLC])` to `expect(warnings).toEqual([])`. The companion paired-pin doc-text test (`expect(doc).toMatch(/Smoothieware-family, not true GRBL/)`) is unchanged -- it still pins the architectural reality, but now the assertion bodies match the validator's new behavior. The flip was zero-line-count net (replace one assertion with one assertion); the comment block above the assertion was extended by ~14 lines to document the Cycle 68 carve-out and link the paired-pin pattern to the [ID-0160] resolution.

Asserts zero warnings against the valid fixture, and asserts a `SMOOTHIEWARE_BAD_M_CODE` warning against an invalid fixture (e.g. a stray `M99`). +9 assertions total; spans the full Smoothieware happy-path matrix.

## Cycle 75 -- 2026-04-26T09:45:00Z -- perf [ID-0153] vitest worker-pool tuning (CLOSE-OUT)

**Focus area**: perf (rotation slot 5 of 6).
**Pull**: [ID-0153] -- vitest worker-pool investigation. Cycle 62 perf-inventory.md closure section ([ID-0091] CLOSE-OUT) filed this as "the remaining hourly-shippable perf opportunity" once per-file shaves were exhausted across Cycles 25 / 41 / 46 / 54 / 62. Cycle 74 close-out flagged perf as the top recommendation with a 12-cycle gap.

### Pre-flight baseline

Captured 2026-04-26 ~09:35Z against working tree HEAD = d4c3732 + Cycles 1-74 WIP:

- `npx tsc --noEmit` -- exit 0.
- `npx vitest run --reporter=basic src/shared` -- 1804 / 77 files in **33.49 s** (re-run 33.60 s; <0.5 % within-config noise band).
- `src/main` and full `npm test` did NOT fit the 45 s sandbox budget at baseline -- this IS the [ID-0066] symptom Cycle 62 framing predicted as the dominant cost.

### Investigation -- controlled A/B/C against identical working tree

| Config | src/shared wall | src/main wall | src/renderer + src/preload | full `npm test` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **A. default fork pool** | 33.49 s | >40 s (didn't fit 45-s sandbox cap) | 5.46 s (Cycle 71 baseline) | >45 s (hit [ID-0066] cap) |
| **B. `pool: 'threads'`, default `singleThread: false`** | 33.56 s | n/a (noise-band match) | n/a | n/a |
| **C. `pool: 'threads'`, `singleThread: true`** | **2.10 s** | **5.07 s** | **2.28 s** | **8.30 s** |

Each cell is a single warm `npx vitest run --reporter=basic <args>` invocation. The src/shared baseline was double-checked (33.60 s on first run, 33.49 s on second) to anchor the noise band.

### Findings

1. The fork-vs-threads pool flavor is NOT the dominant cost. Config B (threads pool, multi-worker) measured within the noise band of config A. Both reuse the per-file worker-startup penalty.
2. The per-file worker-startup penalty IS the dominant cost. vitest's `--reporter=basic` Duration breakdown shows the `prepare` phase at 16.85 s for config B (vs 235 ms for config C). That delta -- 16.6 s of pure overhead per directory-scoped sweep -- is the entire [ID-0066] sandbox-budget overrun.
3. `singleThread: true` reuses one worker across all files. No per-file worker cold-start. The full 4007-test suite drops from >45 s to 8.30 s wall-clock, a **-81 % reduction** with **zero test regressions**.

### Decision

Land config C (`pool: 'threads'` + `poolOptions.threads.singleThread: true`) in `vitest.config.ts`. Pin the config shape with `src/shared/vitest-config-pool.test.ts` (9 tests, 627 ms) so a future cycle cannot silently drop the option block without tripping a test failure.

### Files touched (1 production-code edit + 1 NEW test)

1. **`vitest.config.ts`** -- `pool: 'threads'` + `poolOptions.threads.singleThread: true` block added with 17-line cycle-citing comment block (+29 lines net, 17 -> 46 lines after Python-via-bash recovery from a silent Edit-tool truncation).
2. **NEW `src/shared/vitest-config-pool.test.ts`** (134 lines, 9 tests across 2 describe blocks): imports `../../vitest.config` and runtime-asserts `pool === 'threads'`, `poolOptions.threads.singleThread === true`, plus belt-and-braces shape guards (pool not 'forks' / not 'vmThreads' / typeof === 'string'; singleThread typeof === 'boolean'; poolOptions.threads exists; include glob preserved; testTimeout = 15000 preserved; environment = 'node' preserved).

### Risk + mitigation

Risk: shared module-level state can leak across files within the single thread. A test that mutates `process.env`, a module-level singleton, or `process.cwd()` without afterEach/afterAll cleanup would now affect later files in the same run.

Mitigation 1: the post-flight sweep (4016 / 1 skipped, all green) confirms NO existing test in the suite relies on per-file worker isolation in a way the new config breaks. Future tests that DO mutate process-global state must clean up explicitly.

Mitigation 2: the new pin file `src/shared/vitest-config-pool.test.ts` (9 tests across 2 describes) locks `pool: 'threads'`, `singleThread: true`, `include: ['src/**/*.test.{ts,tsx}']`, `testTimeout: 15000`, and `environment: 'node'` against accidental drift.

Mitigation 3: directory-scoped sweep gates remain unaffected; the pool config applies uniformly whether vitest runs `src/shared` alone or the full suite.

   respectively); the angular kernel scaling (single hit at ia=18 with
   dx=100 chosen to collapse the axial kernel to 1 cell; stockRadius=200
   collapses the angular kernel to a single self-cell, while
   stockRadius=1 expands the angular reach so dia=+/-1 lights up
   neighbours at ia=17 and ia=19); and the rotational continuity at
   the ia=0 / ia=na-1 wrap boundary (single hit at ia=0 with the same
   small-stockRadius parameterization makes both ia=1 AND ia=na-1

  arcMmPerCell < toolRadius for the dia=+/-1 case to actually pass the
  gate. A naive choice of large stockRadius (>>toolRadius/daDeg-rad)
  collapses the angular reach even when the formula yields a nominal
  kernelIa > 1. This is documented in the test 4 in-line comments and
  is a useful future-debug datapoint when paired with the kernel-size
  scaling tests.

### The defect (and why it deserved a post-processing pull, not a test pin)

`applyArcFitting` (`src/main/post-process.ts`) buffers consecutive G1 lines
through `parseG1Point`, fits an XY-plane arc, and emits the result via
`segmentToGcodeLine`. The pipeline is **XY-plane-only**:

  - `parseG1Point` (line 271) only matches `X / Y / Z` regexes; **no rotary
    word extraction**.
  - `segmentToGcodeLine` (line 307) only emits `X Y Z` (plus optional
    `I J K`); the rotary word is gone.

Pre-fix behaviour: when `enableArcFitting: true` was passed for a Carvera
4-axis job (the only 4-axis machine in CLAUDE.md USER CONTEXT), the A-word
on every line in the buffered G1 sequence was **silently stripped** from
the emitted G2/G3 segment. That is a Safety Rule 1 violation: a job that
operator-reviewed a known-good 4-axis toolpath would emit a different
toolpath at runtime, with rotary motion replaced by an XY arc. The first
A-axis collision could destroy the rotary attachment, the workpiece, or
both.

The renderPost call site (line ~729) is **ungated** on `axisCount` -- any
caller that flips `enableArcFitting: true` triggers the bug.

### Files touched (1 production-code edit, 1 NEW contract test file)

1. **`src/main/post-process.ts`** -- 823 -> 856 lines (+33 lines). Two
   coordinated splices via Python-via-bash (the file is over the 800-line
   R1 trigger per `docs/EDIT-WORKFLOW.md` Safety Rule 6):
   - Inserted **`HAS_ROTARY_AXIS_WORD`** module-scope constant +
     12-line JSDoc above `DEFAULT_ARC_TOLERANCE_MM`. The regex
     `/(?:^|\s)[ABC][+-]?\d/` is **over-conservative by design**: false
     positives only inhibit arc fitting (safe direction); false negatives
     would silently strip a rotary word from a fitted arc (unsafe and
     forbidden). The leading anchor `(?:^|\s)` rejects rotary letters
     embedded inside other tokens (e.g. `HAB1` does NOT trigger the
     bypass).
   - Extended the `applyArcFitting` JSDoc with a new "Safety [ID-0173]:
     4-axis rotary bypass" paragraph (12 new lines) explaining the
     XY-plane-only kinematics, the silent-strip risk, the bypass
     contract, the in-scope target machine (Makera Carvera + 4th Axis
     Rotary), and the byte-identical pass-through return shape.
   - Inserted a 6-line bypass guard at the top of the `applyArcFitting`
     function body. When ANY input line matches `HAS_ROTARY_AXIS_WORD`,
     the function returns `lines.slice()` (a fresh array; the
     `[ID-0156] / [ID-0157]` per-machine contract assertions rely on
     callers not mutating the input).
2. **`src/main/post-process-arc-fitting-4axis-safety-contract.test.ts`** --
   **NEW** file, **275 lines / 17 it() blocks across 6 describe blocks**.
   Pure paired-pin shape: each invariant section asserts BOTH the
   documented intent (the JSDoc / comment on `applyArcFitting` and the
   `HAS_ROTARY_AXIS_WORD` constant in `post-process.ts` source text) AND
   the runtime behaviour (against direct `applyArcFitting()` invocation
   plus `renderPost()` integration with the bundled
   `resources/machines/makera-carvera-4axis.json` profile). Doc-vs-code

   - Section 1 -- A-axis bypass (4 it()): single-line A-word, mid-arc

- `npx tsc --noEmit`: exit 0.
- FULL `npm test`: **4226 passed / 1 skipped (4227) / 201 files in 8.65 s**

**The hazard.** `applyCutterCompensation` (post-process.ts line 454) had
NO rotary-axis bypass. Inserting G41 / G42 around a Carvera 4-axis
rotary toolpath that contains A-words is a Safety Rule 1 violation:
cutter compensation (G41 / G42 / G40) is XY-plane-only on every
controller in CLAUDE.md "USER CONTEXT -- TARGET MACHINES" scope (Mach3,
RichAuto A-series, Smoothieware, Klipper). Smoothieware will reject the
program with "comp not allowed during rotary motion"; relaxed firmware
will silently apply diameter compensation while the rotary axis is
moving, producing unpredictable cuts. The hazard is reachable in
production: `src/main/cam-axis4/runner-shims.ts` `extractPostProcessingOpts`
already accepts `cutterCompensation: 'left' | 'right'` on cam-axis4
jobs and `renderPost` calls `applyCutterCompensation` whenever opts
provide a non-`'none'` mode (see post-process.ts lines 768-771).

**The fix.** Mirror the Cycle 85 [ID-0173] pattern. Insert a
`HAS_ROTARY_AXIS_WORD` bypass guard at the top of the
`applyCutterCompensation` body (after the `buildCutterCompLines() ->
null` early-return, before the feed-pattern scan):

```ts
// Safety [ID-0176] -- 4-axis rotary bypass. See JSDoc above.
for (const line of lines) {
  if (HAS_ROTARY_AXIS_WORD.test(line)) {
    return lines.slice()
  }
}
```

The same module-scoped `HAS_ROTARY_AXIS_WORD` constant introduced in
Cycle 85 [ID-0173] is reused unchanged -- no new regex, no new comment
trade-off. JSDoc updated to document the safety bypass and the rotary
axis word (A / B / C) trigger.

  337 lines, **19 it() blocks across 6 describe blocks**:
  1. A-axis (Carvera 4th Axis Rotary) bypass (4 tests): single A-word

**Within-cycle correction (Cycle 92):** the FIRST attempt at writing
the test file produced 2 failing tests against actual implementation
behavior:
1. `estimatedTimeSec` on empty input returns `0`, not `undefined`
   (totalFeedRate defaults to 1200, so 0/1200*60=0; the `undefined`
   branch only triggers when totalFeedRate <= 0).
2. xyBounds tracks ENDPOINT positions only -- a single segment from
   the implicit (0,0,0) origin to (10,0,0) yields minX=maxX=10, not
   minX=0/maxX=10. The implicit origin is never added to bounds
   since the first iteration's `px=0,py=0,pz=0` are local-only and
   bounds update uses the post-move x/y values.

-> Path.write_text` with [ID-0095] uniqueness gates pre-validated

### Changes made

**NEW `src/shared/laguna-vacuum-postlude.ts`** (245 lines)

Pure helper module that turns a `LagunaVacuumZoneAllocation` (from Cycle 98 [ID-0014b]) into deterministic operator-readable G-code preamble + postamble line arrays. The actual `vcarve_mach3.hbs` post-template wiring is deferred to a future cycle per Safety Rule 1 (PostContext schema field + cam-runner wiring + golden-snapshot regeneration is a coherent separate pull).

Public surface:
- 4 marker constants: `LAGUNA_VACUUM_PREAMBLE_OPEN/CLOSE`, `LAGUNA_VACUUM_POSTAMBLE_OPEN/CLOSE`
- 2 warning constants: `LAGUNA_VACUUM_MCODE_WARNING`, `LAGUNA_VACUUM_OUTSIDE_ENVELOPE_WARNING`
- 1 frozen P-number map: `LAGUNA_VACUUM_DIGITAL_OUTPUT_MAP` (column-major: X0Y0->P0, X0Y1->P1, X0Y2->P2, X1Y0->P3, X1Y1->P4, X1Y2->P5)
- 1 options interface: `LagunaVacuumPostludeOptions { enableMach3DigitalOutputs?: boolean }`
- 4 helpers: `lagunaVacuumZonePNumber`, `buildLagunaVacuumPreambleLines`, `buildLagunaVacuumPostambleLines`, `wrapLagunaToolpathWithVacuumBlocks`

Mach3 M64/M65 P-number convention is column-major and lockstep with `LAGUNA_VACUUM_ZONES`. The Laguna Swift 5x10 RichAuto A-series accepts M64/M65 as part of the Mach3-compatible superset already documented in `vcarve_mach3.hbs` (CLAUDE.md target machine #2). M-code emission is **OFF by default** (operator opt-in via `enableMach3DigitalOutputs: true`) because the user's actual digital-output wiring may not match the convention -- emitting unguarded M64 P0 to a controller whose P0 fires the spindle relay instead of vacuum-zone-0 would be a Safety Rule 1 hazard. The always-on portion of the preamble/postamble is semicolon comments only, which Mach3 / RichAuto strips during parsing.

**NEW `src/shared/laguna-vacuum-postlude.test.ts`** (629 lines, 54 it() blocks across 9 describe blocks)

Paired-pin contract:
1. Stable marker constants (6 it()) -- preamble open/close, postamble open/close, M-code warning, outside-envelope warning
2. LAGUNA_VACUUM_DIGITAL_OUTPUT_MAP (3) -- 0..5 unique mapping, column-major order, frozen

4. buildLagunaVacuumPreambleLines happy-path full-sheet (8) -- open/close brackets, "6 of 6 zones engaged" summary, every engaged zone listed, "(none)" sentinel on idle, operator-confirm hint placement, no M64 by default, no outside-envelope warning when in-bounds
5. Partial sheets (2) -- half-sheet "4 of 6", quarter-sheet "2 of 6"
6. Defensive (6) -- zero-engaged still emits markers, zero-engaged + M-codes-on still emits no M64, outside-envelope warning fires, NaN bed-coverage collapses to "0.0%", determinism, no embedded newlines
7. M-code opt-in (4) -- M64 P0..P5 for full-sheet, warning above M64, inline comment names zone, half-sheet P-numbers match engaged-zone column-major order
8. buildLagunaVacuumPostambleLines (7) -- markers, release count, M65 not M64, P-number order, default omits M65, zero-engaged emits no M65, determinism
9. wrapLagunaToolpathWithVacuumBlocks (7) -- toolpath bytes preserved verbatim in middle slice, ordering, length-additive, empty toolpath, M-code option pass-through, default M64/M65-free, readonly toolpath input accepted
10. Cross-helper invariants (3) -- M64 + M65 count == 2 x engaged across all planforms, marker pair 1:1, every wrapped line is a comment / M-code / toolpath byte
11. JSDoc paired-pin (5) -- module exports the full named surface, Safety Rule 1 cited, [ID-0020-followup] tracking ID cited, P-number map spelled out, wiring-confirm warning present

**In-cycle assertion fix.** Pin (31) -- meshRadialMin tracks the smallest real hit across the whole grid -- initial draft was wrong about ray semantics. First-write expected `meshRadialMin ~= 14` based on incorrect mental model that the heightmap's rays only originate from the +Z direction. The actual contract is that `buildCylindricalHeightmap` sweeps ALL angular cells `ia in [0, na)`; plates are 2-sided so the same z=8 plate is hit from BOTH the +Z side (A=0, blocked by z=14, records r=14) AND the -Z side (A=180, hits z=8 first because it's closer to oz=-50 with t=58 vs t=64 for z=14, records r=8). Global min across the full grid === 8, NOT 14. Pin re-written to document the 2-sided ray convention as the actual contract, with a tolerance band (7.9 < meshRadialMin < 8.1) plus hitCount > 0 + clampedCount === 0 guards. Patched via Python-via-bash `str.replace` with `assert count == 1` uniqueness gate per [ID-0095]. Lesson logged: when pinning ray-cast aggregate stats, the +Z-side reasoning that works for per-cell pins (where ix/ia are specified) does NOT apply to global aggregates -- those reflect ALL angular directions.

**In-cycle fixes.** THREE assertion-text fixes (NOT [ID-0067] datapoints, NOT Edit-tool fires) on the FIRST focused-vitest run. Root cause: I misread the Y - Z swap convention in `shop-stock-bounds.ts`. The swap applies to the user-input fields scale/position (scY = t.scale.z, fy = ... + t.position.z), NOT to the model coordinate axes themselves -- at identity transform, corners carry (model X, model Y, model Z) into Three.js (X, Y, Z) 1:1. I had originally written assertions that swapped the corner-extent identification (claiming Three.js Y carries model Z; actually it carries model Y). All 3 fixes via Python-via-bash str.replace with [ID-0095] count==1 uniqueness gates: (1) corner-ordering test on (10, 20, 30) -- (-5,-10,-15) not (-5,-15,-10); (2) bounds test on (80, 60, 12) -- Y bounds +/-30 not +/-6; (3) 90 deg X-rotation test -- max |Y| = 1, max |Z| ~ 0 (not the reverse). Lesson: the swap is on the user-input *fields* (scale.z drives Y extent magnitude, position.z offsets Y origin), but the model corner emission is straight (X, Y, Z) -> (X, Y, Z). Source-text whitelist tests in section (I) now nail down the exact swap-on-input arithmetic so future readers won't make the same mistake.

It does NOT -- TS optional parameters (`?`) keep the parameter in Function.length; only an explicit default value `opts: T = {}` removes it. Both functions have arity 1; updated to `.toBe(1)` with explanatory inline comment.
2. **`/\bM3\b/` collision with operator-prose comment in preflight check.** The preamble of `generateCarveraPreflightCheck` includes the comment `; Spindle speed is set but NOT started (no M3).` which legitimately names the AVOIDED opcode in operator-facing prose. The pin still proves no M3 / M03 G-code is emitted as an executable spindle-on command -- the original safety intent is preserved with tighter regex application.
3. **`/M30/` collision with JSDoc safety framing.** The module-level JSDoc deliberately states `M2 ends a program (NEVER M30 -- M30 deletes the file from the SD card)`. The Safety-Rule-1 pin is that M30 is never *emitted*, not that the word never appears. Tightened to a 3-pattern check: no `'M30'` in single-quoted string literals, no backtick-M30-backtick in template literals, no `'M30 ` or backtick-M30 followed by a space (covering G-code-emission patterns). The pin still defends against any actual M30 emission while admitting the operator-facing safety framing.
4. **TS2352 `readonly ["x","y","z"]` vs `('x'|'y'|'z'|'a')[]` cast widening.** The frozen-input safety test cast `Object.freeze([...] as const)` directly to the mutable axis-array type, which TS rejected as insufficient overlap. Added the `as unknown as` two-step widening -- the test's intent is to prove the function accepts a frozen array without throwing, which the assignability widening preserves at runtime.

Target: `src/renderer/dashboard/WorkshopDashboard.tsx` (Gap #10, ~520 LoC) was using BEM classes (`workshop-dashboard__card`, `__grid`, `__dot`, `__chip`, etc.) but **zero matching CSS rules** existed in any stylesheet — the dashboard was rendering with browser-default styling (unstyled divs, no grid, no card borders, no chip pills, no status-dot positioning). Three tasks, all confined to renderer + CSS + the dashboard test file.
- **Baseline**: `npm test` → 13689 passed / 0 failed / 2 skipped (343 files; identical to HEAD a108f94). `npm run typecheck` → clean (exit 0).
- **Changes**:
  - `src/renderer/styles/manufacture.css` — appended ~110-line `Workshop Dashboard (Gap #10)` block at EOF (line 1296 → 1465). All rules use `tokens.css` design tokens (no hard-coded colors): `.workshop-dashboard` + `__header`/`__title`/`__sub` (region wrapper); `__grid` (3-column desktop, 1-column ≤900px); `__card` (border, radius-lg, hover lift via elevation-1); `__card--current` (accent border + focus-ring); `__card-header`/`__card-titleblock`/`__card-name`/`__card-subtitle`; `__badge` (Active pill, accent-dim background); `__status-row`/`__dot`/`__status-label`; `__chip-row`/`__chip`/`__chip--filename`; `__last-row` (dl flex)/`__last-key`/`__last-val`/`__last-file` (mono)/`__last-status`; `__action-row` (margin-top:auto so the quick-action sticks to card bottom regardless of card height variance) + `__action` (width 100%).
  - `src/renderer/dashboard/WorkshopDashboard.tsx` — two surgical edits:
    1. `StatusDot` inline style trimmed from 6 properties (display, width, height, borderRadius, backgroundColor, marginRight) to 1 (backgroundColor only). Geometry and spacing now live in `.workshop-dashboard__dot` in manufacture.css. The dynamic per-status color stays inline because it is driven by the `DASHBOARD_STATUS_COLORS` map's 8 discrete kinds.
    2. `WorkshopCard`'s root `<section>` gained `role="listitem"` to pair with the existing `role="list"` on `.workshop-dashboard__grid`. ARIA requires listitem children when an ancestor declares list; without the pairing, screen readers stop announcing the list.
  - `src/renderer/dashboard/WorkshopDashboard.test.tsx` — appended two new describe groups (4 new it() blocks) at EOF:
    - **List/listitem ARIA pairing**: pins (a) grid container `role="list"` survives, (b) exactly 3 `role="listitem"` occurrences in the rendered HTML, (c) every card section carries listitem regardless of job state (mixed-state fixture).
    - **StatusDot inline-style scope**: pins that the dot's inline style contains only `background-color` — no width, height, border-radius, or margin leak in. Locks the token-scoped contract so future edits can not regress to inline geometry.
- **Tests added**: **+4 it() blocks** in `WorkshopDashboard.test.tsx` (3 list/listitem a11y + 1 token-scope inline-style pin). Focused: `npx vitest run src/renderer/dashboard/WorkshopDashboard.test.tsx` → 27 passed (was 23) in 37 ms.

- **G-code path safety**: **N/A** — zero touches under `engines/cam/`, `src/main/cam-*`, `resources/posts/**`, `resources/machines/**`, or the post-process pipeline. Diff is confined to one CSS file + one TSX component + one TSX test file, all under `src/renderer/`. Safety Rule 1 preserved by construction; `gcode-safety` skill invocation not required.
- **Three-machine impact**: INDIRECT — the dashboard surfaces per-machine status for all three (Laguna Swift 5x10, Creality K2 Plus, Makera Carvera). The CSS makes the existing three-card layout visually legible without changing any behavior, IPC, or G-code. ## PRE-LAUNCH SUB-AGENT STACK — 2026-06-01 — pre-real-world-testing readiness

> User-directed multi-workflow run. NOT a numbered rotation cycle.
> Goal: "set up a sub agent stack to handle progress work on this app
> and run them all until we have everything done we can before real
> world testing." Three sequential workflows + one inline phase.

- **Pattern**: 8 parallel scouts → adversarial per-finding verifier → synthesizer
- **Scope**: Machine profiles, post-processors, OrcaSlicer profiles, IPC test coverage, security (npm audit), docs, first-launch samples
- **Output**: 27 raw findings → **23 verified real** → ranked 19-item punch list (5 G-code-touching mechanical, 5 CSS-only mechanical, 1 SettingsUI mechanical, 6 docs, 1 INI comment, 1 regression-pin coverage, 3 deferred design-effort)

### Workflow A — Apply mechanical fixes (task wze4vj1hg, ~18.4 min, 12 agents, 865K tokens)
- **Pattern**: 11 parallel fix agents grouped by target file (to avoid concurrent-write collisions) + 1 sequential validator
- **Apply phase**: all 11 returned . Files changed across machine profiles, posts, CSS, SettingsView, docs, INI, regression pins.
- **Validate phase**: caught **7 regressions** — but ALL were test pins encoding the *old wrong* spindle ranges. The agents correctly bumped the JSONs to CLAUDE.md spec; the test pins needed manual reconciliation.
- **Inline reconciliation** (main loop, post-workflow): Updated 4 test files (, , , ) to assert the new CLAUDE.md-correct ranges (Laguna 6000-24000, Carvera 3-axis 13000-15000). Bumped clamp-test inputs so each clamp branch is still exercised (Laguna max-clamp uses 25000 → clamps 24000; min-clamp uses 5000 → clamps 6000). Regenerated 2 vacuum-postlude snapshots via . Net post-flight: 13611/0/2 + tsc clean.
- **Net Δ vs Cycle-233 post-flight**: -82 vitest (5-axis test surface deletions) + 3 new spindle-pin tests + 4 dashboard-test count shift. Zero regressions.

### gcode-safety skill invocation (inline)
- **Verdict**: SAFE for all three target machines.
- **(a) Laguna widening (8k-18k → 6k-24k)**: reduces false-positive clamps; HW supports the wider range;  is a monotone clamp with operator-visible warnings on both edges.
- **(b) Carvera 3-axis floor bump (6k → 13k)**: UPGRADES safety; rejects sub-spec RPM that would damage the 200W spindle; explicit  warning surfaces the substitution.
- **(c) Fanuc/Siemens CPS → cnc_generic_mm.hbs fallback**: emits valid 3-axis CNC G-code with explicit G21/G90/G17/M30 and a multi-line UNVERIFIED warning header. Safe on any 3-axis Fanuc/Siemens control. Loss of 5-axis capability is the intended My-Shop-Only scope reduction.
- **Side fix landed**: The gcode-safety reference files (, ) encoded the *old wrong* spindle ranges. Updated header + envelope table + fixture recipe entries to match the corrected profiles.

- Switched from fan-out to inline because (a) the readiness report benefits from full session context that a sub-agent would lose, and (b) the 3 remaining items (vitest 3→4, Carvera 4-axis schema, post rename) are genuine design-effort that needs user decisions, not mechanical work agents can apply.
